title: Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year Fiscal 2026 Results Reported by Compass Minerals
summary: Compass Minerals hosted its fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year earnings call, reporting a return to profitability with net income of $17.5 million
body_markdown:
#### Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year Fiscal 2026 Results Reported by Compass Minerals


Compass Minerals hosted its fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year earnings call, reporting a return to profitability with net income of $17.5 million for fiscal 2026 compared with a net loss of $79.8 million in fiscal 2025.


“For the second consecutive year, we delivered on our commitments and made meaningful progress strengthening the earnings capacity and financial position of Compass Minerals,” said Edward C. Dowling Jr., president and CEO. “Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA was up 18%, we returned to positive net income, substantially improved Plant Nutrition profitability and reduced net leverage to 3.2 times. Importantly, these results reflect progress in the areas we can control: operating reliability, production efficiency, pricing discipline and cost management. We enter fiscal 2027 from a stronger operational and commercial position. Our North American highway bid season produced approximately 12% expected pricing improvement, while guaranteed terms increased to 78% of the committed U.S. portfolio from 65% last year. We expect stronger pricing, improved customer mix and continued reductions in per-ton production costs to more than offset lower planned salt volumes and higher fuel-related logistics costs. At the midpoint of our outlook, adjusted EBITDA is expected to increase approximately 15%, Salt adjusted EBITDA per ton is expected to improve more than 29%, and Salt adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to expand approximately 400 basis points. While there is more work ahead, the progress achieved over the past two years demonstrates that our focus on disciplined execution is producing measurable results. Our fiscal 2027 priorities are straightforward: operate safely and reliably, continue reducing unit costs, convert improved pricing into stronger margins, complete our highest-return capital projects and use improved earnings to further strengthen the balance sheet.”


Other fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year results reported include:


- Adjusted net income improved to $32.5 million, or $0.76 per diluted share, compared with an adjusted net loss of $20.1 million, or $(0.48) per diluted share, in the prior year.


- Adjusted EBITDA increased 18% to $235.1 million, exceeding the company’s previous guidance range midpoint. Excluding the prior-year non-cash Fortress gain, adjusted EBITDA increased approximately 23%.


- Salt segment adjusted EBITDA increased 8% to $235.8 million, while adjusted EBITDA per ton improved approximately 7% to $21.72, as pricing gains and lower per-unit production costs more than offset higher fuel-driven logistics costs and a soft winter in the U.K.


- Plant Nutrition adjusted EBITDA increased 57% to $54.8 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding approximately 950 basis points to 26.4%, driven by higher pricing and lower per-unit costs at Ogden.


- The fourth-quarter net loss was $8.1 million compared to $7.2 million in the prior-year period, as a narrower pre-tax loss was more than offset by higher income tax expense. Fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA increased 5% to $43.5 million, supported by a 16% increase in Salt segment adjusted EBITDA.


- Total debt declined $65 million to $767.2 million, while net debt declined $23.9 million to $748.6 million, reducing net leverage to 3.2 times from 3.9 times a year earlier.


You can find additional details in the press release and the Fiscal 2026 Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year Business Update posted in the[Investor Relations](https://investors.compassminerals.com/investors-relations/events-and-presentations/presentations/default.aspx) section of the company website.
